Covered areas

6 suburbs, each with its own page

What changes between them is the housing stock, the access and what the ground turns out to be once the first metre is off.

Newcastle

A long industrial history close to dense older housing, which makes contaminated ground and unknown fill real considerations.

Charlestown

Established post-war housing on sloping blocks, with redevelopment pressure around the centre.

Merewether

Older coastal housing on tight blocks, weathered by the exposure and almost all of it pre 1990.

Warners Bay

Lakefront and lakeside blocks with low lying ground in parts, which affects excavation and fill.

Belmont

Older lakeside stock with a lot of original fibro, on blocks where access varies street by street.

Maitland

Inland flood plain stock, where flood affected land and older timber and fibro housing shape most scopes.

The ground and the site

What actually decides the price here

We do not have a published geological record we are willing to assert for every block in Newcastle and Lake Macquarie, so this page does not pretend to one. What does shape the work here is observable, and it is the same list every time:

  • Industrial and post-industrial land. Newcastle has a long industrial history, which makes contaminated ground and fill of unknown origin a real consideration rather than a theoretical one.
  • Older housing stock across the lake suburbs. Charlestown, Warners Bay and Belmont carry a lot of pre 1990 construction, so hazardous materials surveys are routine.
  • Mine subsidence districts in parts of the area. Which is a planning and engineering matter that affects what can be built and how, and it is worth confirming before a design is fixed.
  • Lakefront and low lying ground. Which affects drainage, excavation and what can be used as fill.

A geotechnical report, where one exists, settles the ground question for a particular property far better than any regional statement can.

Digging here

Four conditions, and each one is dug differently

The geology named here is the published regional record. What any particular block is made of has to be found by looking at it.

Topsoil and unknown fill

On former industrial land this is the first real question, because what is in the fill determines the destination and much of the price.

How it comes out
Tested and classified before it moves rather than after. Mixing it with clean material does not reclassify it.
What does it
Excavator working to a control plan, lined trucks where the classification requires it.

Contaminated ground

A live possibility rather than a remote one here, and it is a specialist disposal question rather than a digging one.

How it comes out
Delineated, excavated, removed to a facility licensed to receive that classification, then validated.
What does it
Excavator under a control plan, with remediation able to sit on the same contract.

Stiffer natural ground

Below the fill. What it is varies across the area, so the method is set by what the dig actually finds.

How it comes out
Dug with a toothed bucket, reassessed as it goes down.
What does it
Midi to large excavator with a toothed bucket.

Rock and hard layers

Where they appear, and they are priced separately from earthworks for the same reason everywhere else.

How it comes out
Hammered and priced by the cubic metre at an agreed rate.
What does it
Large excavator with a hydraulic hammer.

Newcastle and Lake Macquarie questions

What people here ask us first

How do you handle ground that might be contaminated?
It is tested and classified before it moves, then taken to a facility licensed to receive that classification. On former industrial land around Newcastle this is a normal part of the job rather than an exception, and remediation can be quoted on the same contract.
Does mine subsidence affect what you can do?
Parts of the area sit in mine subsidence districts, which is a planning and engineering matter affecting what can be built and how. It is worth confirming for a particular property before a design is fixed.
Do you work around the lake as well as in Newcastle itself?
Yes. Charlestown, Warners Bay, Belmont and the surrounding suburbs are part of the same coverage, along with Maitland inland.
What has to happen before a demolition can start?
A hazardous materials survey, removal and clearance of anything the survey finds, written confirmation that water, sewer, gas, electricity and telecommunications are disconnected, and the approval in place. The structure is the last part, not the first.
Is the slab and the footings included?
Only if that is what the new build needs. Sometimes a slab stays and is built over and sometimes it all comes out, and it is worth settling with the builder before the quote rather than afterwards.
Does the asbestos work sit under your demolition licence?
No. Demolition licence AD214737 covers the structure. Removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists and clearance by an independent licensed assessor, because the assessor has to be independent of whoever did the removal. All of it is scheduled as a single job.
